decisions.question: Probability check: when it is promoted (PC-07), may it only scale position size, or also veto trades below an expected-R floor?
decisions.recommendation: Size only at first: a veto starves the book (goal: at least a couple of trades a week).
decisions.answer: Owner 2026-10-31: size AND block, with bands on the calibrated P(TP hit). Block below ~30%. 30–60%: trade at reduced size (0.5x). 60–85%: normal size, rising toward 1.25x. ~90% and above: allocate more (up to 1.5x), always inside S3 caps. High probability should also manage the trade: partial take-profit at TP50 and/or lock break-even (new task PC-08). The bands are frozen only once PC-07 shows the probabilities are calibrated. Caveat to check at PC-07: P(full TP) falls with wider targets, so a fixed 30% block could reject every 3R trade even when its expected R is positive.

decisions.question: Text scorer for central-bank statements: which candidates may the bake-off (TX-01) use, and may an LLM polish the morning briefing?
decisions.options: Encoders only (FinBERT, FinBERT-tone, CentralBankRoBERTa) · + FOMC-RoBERTa (CC BY-NC, research only) · + Claude via API (metered)
decisions.recommendation: All of them in the bake-off; FOMC-RoBERTa for research only; Claude via API on post-cutoff statements, cost logged. Briefing polish off until the deterministic text is trusted.
decisions.answer: Owner 2026-10-31: test them all, as recommended (FinBERT is just one probability model among several). FOMC-RoBERTa for research only (CC BY-NC); Claude counts only on statements after its training cutoff. Briefing polish stays off for now. Confirm if this reading is wrong.
